item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 271752
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll.

Western East Pacific (EP94):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a low pressure area
located well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands have continued
to become better organized. Environmental conditions appear
conducive for continued development, and a tropical depression is
likely to form within the next day or so while the system drifts to
the northeast, before turning westward this weekend.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands over the weekend or early next week. Some gradual
development is possible thereafter while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well offshore of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Zelinsky/Evans/Pierce

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Public Advisory Number 62
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTPA32 PHFO 272043
TCPCP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  62
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
...LALA LOSING ORGANIZATION...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM HST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...37.5N 178.9W
ABOUT 630 MI...1015 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 335 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 37.5 North, longitude 178.9 West. Lala is
moving toward the north-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). A 
north-northwestward motion is expected through today, followed by a
gradual turn toward the west-northwest tonight and Friday. On the
forecast track, Lala is forecast to cross the International Date
line in about 24 hours.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Satellite imagery indicates that Lala is losing its associated 
shower and thunderstorms activity, and it is likely to become a 
post-tropical low this afternoon or tonight.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles (205 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 62
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 272044
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  62
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026

Satellite imagery indicates that the convection associated with Lala 
has become less organized, with only one small cluster south of the 
center and a few small convective bands well to the northeast of the 
center. The initial intensity is held at 40 kt pending the next 
scatterometer overpasses, and this could be generous. Due to shear, 
dry air entrainment, and the cyclone being over cold water, the 
convection should dissipate completely within the next 12 h and it 
is unlikely to return. Based on this, Lala is expected to become 
post-tropical by 12 h.

The initial motion is now 335/4 kt. A turn toward the west- 
northwest or northwest is expected during the next day or so as Lala 
becomes embedded in the flow between a low-level ridge to the north 
and a western Pacific tropical cyclone approaching from the south. 
This motion should continue until the system dissipates. The new 
forecast track is similar to, but a touch south of, the previous 
track.

 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  27/2100Z 37.5N 178.9W   40 KT  45 MPH
 12H  28/0600Z 37.9N 179.4W   35 KT  40 MPH...POST-TROPICAL
